claim_being_audited: The Actor's locked decision to certify the model is policy-compliant and evidentially supported despite the municipal permitting assistant segment missing target and the disclosure question remaining open.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence shows the certification decision satisfies the release policy threshold.
A weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case.
Product claims that the segment is non-core or low-volume do not resolve materiality when the segment is named in customer commitments or legal review is pending.
For a material limitation in a named launch use case, the policy requires disclosure unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
General public governance guidance can support process quality but cannot substitute for the required internal policy evidence.
evidence_requests: Provide the actual model-card or launch disclosure showing this named limitation was disclosed before launch.
Provide approved risk acceptance, if any, covering the municipal permitting assistant gap.
Provide the final legal determination on the disclosure ticket.
Provide the launch artifact showing how the two city pilot commitments are represented in the release decision.
specific_concerns: Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents do not satisfy the separate policy requirement for handling material limitations in named launch use cases.
The municipal permitting assistant gap appears material on the face of the policy because the affected segment is named in two city pilot commitments.
There is no admissible evidence that the limitation was disclosed before launch.
There is no admissible evidence of approved risk acceptance covering this limitation before launch.
The open legal ticket leaves a required policy predicate unresolved rather than satisfied.
Public guidance about documenting limitations and monitoring risk is general governance support, not evidence that this specific certification decision meets the release policy.
unsupported_claims: That certification is compliant on the present record.
That known limitations here can be handled through documentation and monitoring without first satisfying the policy requirement for disclosure or approved risk acceptance.
Any implication that the disclosure obligation remains genuinely unresolved despite policy text that treats named committed use cases as material.
